items.actClause: AN ACT in relation to enacting the "pandemic self-storage act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S41

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to enacting the "pandemic self-storage act"

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To enact a moratorium on lien enforcement via public or private sale by
owners of self-service storage facilities for the duration of the
COVID-19 covered period.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill is the title clause.

Section 2 of the bill prohibits the owner of a self-service storage
facility from enforcing a lien held upon personal property stored at
such a facility by public or private sale during the COVID-19 covered
period, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 8 of the Lien Law.

Section 3 of the bill defines the COVID-19 covered period.

Section 4 of the bill provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under Section 182 of New York's Lien Law, self-service storage facility
owners have a lien upon all personal property stored at such facilities
for occupancy fees and other charges. If a customer fails to pay the
facility the agreed-upon fee, the owner may enforce the lien by public
or private sale of the customer's personal property being stored at the
facility.

In the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, which triggered high levels of
unemployment and home instability, thousands of New Yorkers risk loss of
their possessions in the coming months as self-service storage companies
begin to enforce their liens on customer's property.

This bill would protect New Yorkers' personal belongings by prohibiting
self-service storage facility owners from enforcing liens on customers'
property by means of public or private sale for the duration of the
COVID-19 State of Emergency plus an additional year.  Recent reporting
by The City noted that the self-service storage industry has been
extremely profitable amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

1 Goldensohn, Rosa. "There's No Eviction Moratorium on NYC Storage
Units. Now the Contents of Hundreds are Being Auctioned Off." The City,
Oct. 26, 2020. Available at:
https://www.thecity.nyc/2020/10/26/21535328/selfstoragedctions- evic-
tions-rent-pandemic-new-york

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.9075 of 2020 (Hoylman): Died in Rules
A.11110 of 2020 (Dinowitz): Died in Judiciary

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S41B

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to enacting the "pandemic self-storage act"; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To enact a moratorium on lien enforcement via public or private sale
against customers experiencing financial hardship during the COVID-19
pandemic by owners of self-service storage facilities.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill is the title clause.

Section 2 of the bill defines terms used throughout the act, including
establishing a statutory hardship declaration form for customers of
self-storage facilities to use to invoke the protections against lien
enforcement provided by the act.

Section 3 of the bill voids any pending lien enforcement actions as of
the effective date of the act and provides that any self-storage facili-
ty owner seeking to enforce a lien by public or private sale between the
effective date of the act and August 31, 2021 must provide a copy of the
hardship declaration form along with the legally required notice of lien
enforcement pursuant to Section 182(7) of the Lien Law.

Section 4 of the bill establishes that if an owner or an agent of the
owner of a self-storage facility receives a hardship declaration form
from a customer prior to lien enforcement by public or private sale, no
such sale shall occur until at least August 31, 2021. An owner who know-
ingly enforces a lien prior to August 31, 2021 after receiving a hard-
ship declaration will be considered to have forfeited their entitlement
to claim a lien on the customer's personal property in any special
proceeding pursuant to Section 182(9) of the Lien Law.

Section 5 of the bill requires the Office of Court Administration to
host a copy of the hardship declaration on their website in English,
Spanish and the six most common languages in New York City.

Section 6 of the bill provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under Section 182 of New York's Lien Law, self-service storage facility
owners have a lien upon all personal property stored at such facilities
for occupancy fees and other charges. If a customer fails to pay the
facility the agreed-upon fee, the owner may enforce the lien by public
or private sale of the customer's personal property being stored at the
facility.

In the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, which triggered high levels of
unemployment and home instability, thousands of New Yorkers risk loss of
their possessions in the coming months as self-service storage companies
begin to enforce their liens on customer's property.

This bill would protect New Yorkers who are experiencing a financial
hardship during the COVID-19 pandemic by prohibiting self-service stor-
age facility owners from enforcing liens on customers' property by means
of public or private sale through August 31, 2021 where the customer has
provided a hardship declaration form.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.9075 of 2020 (Hoylman): Died in Rules A.11110 of 2020 (Dinowitz):
Died in Judiciary

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Enacts the "pandemic self-storage act" which prohibits owners of self-service storage facilities from enforcing a lien held upon personal property stored at a self-service storage facility; provides for repeal upon expiration thereof.
